source_audit.decode_cap: Cap applied only after fitting; probability output takes precedence; full-decoding and segment paths match audited source loop and formatting behavior.
source_audit.em: Preserves callback order and last live callback side effects; observer errors propagate.
source_audit.snapshot: Finite numbers serialize at round-trip precision; NaN/Inf labels match instrumented-reference classification; final flush propagates errors.
source_audit.input: Rust parser retains kseq ASCII aliases, boundary behavior and ignored FASTQ qualities. Runtime safety rejects malformed/empty/non-ASCII inputs and unsupported supplied-grid/divergence combinations.

resolved_findings: Hardlinked input and new-path sink aliases could truncate data or corrupt outputs; inode and resolved-parent comparisons now reject them.
Bootstrap trace could alias report or snapshot; all active sinks now checked pairwise.
Dangling final symlink could bypass path identity; rejected before writes.
Input stdin and default stdout aliases were not represented as paths; Linux fd identities now included.
Round-zero snapshot buffered-write errors were ignored; Observer.finish now flushes and propagates failure.
Round-zero/live-model nonfinite values could go unreported; initialization and model fields now included in warnings.
documented_limitations_to_preserve: Linux/libm/system-zlib tested stack only; no CUDA or acceleration claim.
Decimal/exponent finite numeric input; C hex-float tokens excluded.
Empty, malformed and non-ASCII sequence input rejected.
At most 255 parameter groups; bootstrap raw-total restricted to legacy signed-int stopping range.
Explicit supplied-grid/divergence combinations and parameter-file -T without a final divergence value rejected.
Pre-create alias checks do not claim protection against concurrent adversarial filesystem replacement.
coordination_note: A previous shared-release rebuild invalidated a concurrent numerical validation attempt. That interrupted attempt is not evidence for numerical parity. The numerical agent is validating an immutable executable copy separately; this targeted review performed no rebuild.
